doc.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022

title: Grants and arts panels
summary: She says whether progressive work gets grants depends on the panel and the quality of work, citing the New York Foundation for the Arts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Yes, it’s usually the other way around. You’ve had, been a recipient of a number of grants over the years. An acquaintance of mine said something once that sounded true but I’m not sure and that was organizations don’t give out grants for arts that aren’t cutting edge. You’re not going to get a grant to compose music like Mozart or to play more bebop. Do you think that’s true?
As far as my experience goes it depends who’s on the panel.

It depends who’s on the panel. I know I’ve been asked many times to write things for people applying for grants and to my knowledge no one I’ve, you know, written things for has actually gotten a grant. And then I just get infuriated because a lot of these people are just brilliant people. I’ve been on a couple of panels, arts panels. And I think it’s really about the quality of the music because I know the New York Foundation for the Arts Panel, when that was happening we all kind of agreed on some very progressive

stuff and then there was like some very beautiful choral stuff that was more traditional. So I don’t think that’s true across the board. I would say it has more to do — at least in my experience — with the quality of the work.
